items.title: Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory
items.description: Learn More: https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n A cloud-based assistant can remember what it sees, hears, and is told, but only by staying connected and sending that data to a remote server. In our new short course, Building AI Assistants with On-Device Memory, built in partnership with Qdrant and taught by Dylan Couzon, Developer Experience Engineer at Qdrant, you'll learn to store and search an assistant's memories locally, so nothing has to leave the device. In this course, you'll learn how to: - Build a local memory system that stores, retrieves, filters, and forgets text and image memories. - Build an offline assistant that recalls experiences across text, voice, and images. - Teach an AI application to recognize new objects from stored examples without retraining a model. - Run the on-device AI assistant on a local machine, including Mac, Windows, and Linux. This course also includes our new AI coding lab, so you can practice building with an AI coding agent from the DeepLearning.AI mobile app. Enroll Now:https://bit.ly/4AlVW2n

items.title: Where the Junior Dev Jobs Went
items.description: Why are junior developers struggling right now? The jobs didn't disappear, they moved. The routine code juniors used to get hired for was the bottom rung of the ladder, and AI sawed it off. That work moved up the stack toward the things AI can't do, landing at the mid and senior level. The mistake most people make: optimizing for the job that existed three years ago, not today. #techwithtim #softwareengineering #techjobs

items.creator: DeepLearning.AI
items.title: Full Course: Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents
items.description: Vibe coding is fast, but it often produces code that doesn't match what you asked for. Spec-driven development is the disciplined alternative: write a clear markdown spec defining what to build, and let your coding agent implement it. Earn your certificate here: https://bit.ly/4ArdsT3 You'll learn to: - Write a project constitution defining mission, tech stack, and roadmap - Plan, implement, and validate features using a spec as the agent's guide - Introduce SDD to a legacy codebase - Package your workflow into an agent skill that's portable across agents and IDEs Spec-Driven Development with Coding Agents is built in partnership with JetBrains and taught by Paul Everitt, Developer Advocate at JetBrains. Recommended: basic familiarity with a programming language and experience with LLM-based coding tools.

items.description: Scientists just discovered a new wild cat species and the internet is going insane 🐈 Meet the Tilcayo tiger cat newly! It’s small, elusive, and has been hiding from humans this entire time. New species discoveries like this are becoming more common as AI-assisted field research and satellite tracking reach places humans never could before. The wild is still full of things we haven’t found yet. When I saw a viral video by @fatiihh.shn of his cat, I had to make this with the new cat spieces 🐱 credit to @fatiihh.shn on IG for this amazing idea! Wdyt? Is it cute or scary?

items.description: Get Kylon for your own business, first month FREE ($100 value), sign up through: https://app.kylon.io/c/p_rPCmMI32cB6JrauRRYrJIRujz5Iz30 To deploy Kylon for clients, book a call: https://cal.com/team/kylon/meet-kylon Want an AI Makeover for YOUR Business? 👉🏻 https://bit.ly/aimakeover Follow me on Instagram to see behind the scenes: 🤳🏼 https://instagram.com/liamottley Work with Josh: https://www.thomasandcointernational.com/ Josh's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/joshthomas Josh's YouTube: @joshthomas-co In this AI Makeover, I head to Marbella to help Josh Thomas, the founder of Thomas & Co, one of the fastest growing accountancy firms in the UK, fix the most boring job in his business. 25 of his accountants spend more than half of every working week filling in working papers by hand, over 20 hours a week each, and with the whole industry racing to put AI first, we had four days to build a system that could do it for them. The catch: I've never worked a day of accounting in my life, and by law a human still has to sign off every number. Four days later we ran the first working paper through it, to see if we'd actually given 25 accountants their week back...
